why: The pilot's final call, 2026-09-20: six of final-v1's seven spell swaps, Hellkite Courser KEPT, and exactly one land change. Marang River Regent is dropped because the Courser is itself a 6/5 Dragon that deploys the commander with haste and no commander tax — a six-mana burst Marang does not replicate. With Marang gone the deck loses its second double-blue card, so the whole ten-land pass built to support it is unnecessary: measured on the untouched 35 lands, the six swaps leave EVERY colour gap identical to the sleeved list. The one land change is the deck's standing red shortfall, not these swaps.

commits.message: Six spell swaps, Courser kept, one land: a Forest for a Mountain

staged.why: A red planeswalker whose loyalty needs defending, for a one-mana counter. Almost every creature in the 99 has power 4 or greater, so ferocious is live from the first Dragon and it counters outright rather than taxing. This is the 'I now have zero responses' problem answered directly.

Six mana to draw off a creature that has to survive first is a win-more card that does nothing while you are being attacked. Mithril Coat costs three, has flash, is itself indestructible, and auto-attaches to a legendary on arrival. Best performer in the 177-game Forge run: cast 40, activated 35.

A one-mana tutor that finds a creature and puts it on top is card SELECTION in a deck that already finds threats easily. Asceticism gives the whole board hexproof plus a regenerate outlet — the only mass protection in the package.

Return grants NO trample, so one chump block stops the pump mode; its real job was always the draw half. Steel Hellkite is colourless, flies, and destroys every nonland permanent at a chosen mana value belonging to anyone it hit. Second-best in the Forge run: cast 36, activated 53.
Eight mana for a token engine that must connect first, for six mana of flash, flying and a counterspell on a body that lets you cast the countered spell yourself.

An anthem needs a wide board and this deck builds a tall one. Whirlwing gives flash to your sorceries and Dragons, which is what lets you hold mana up instead of tapping out and telegraphing — the pilot's own diagnosis.

The deck's STANDING red shortfall, not something these swaps caused: red is 54.5% of the pips on 29 sources against a Karsten target of 36, and it reads the same on the sleeved list. Green is the only colour at or over target, and mana-fit names this Forest its one cut candidate. A Mountain is free, always untapped, never dead, and a fetch target for four of the eight fetches.

Plus one land, a Forest for a Mountain, against the deck's standing red shortfall.

proposal.forced_reason: The pilot has sleeved it and directed the merge. The objective I set (kill_by_8 >= 0.85) is not met and it was a poor choice on my part: this branch trades two fat threats for two answers, so a CLOCK measure is the wrong endpoint for it. The honest reading is the one the goldfish gives — killed by t10 95 -> 96 per 100 better, damage @t10 -4.07 worse as the priced cost, everything else inside the noise — plus the deterministic fact that the six spell swaps demand nothing of the manabase at all.
